item.summary: This notebook synthesizes research proposing that AI failure states—often attributed to agentic autonomy—are more accurately conceptualized as governance failures arising from the delegation of moral authority. By analyzing historical models of artificial agency, the work shifts the focus from machine capability to the accountability arrangements established by human designers.
item.title: Synthesis: Governance Failures in AI Obedience

review.alternative: Failures could arise from emergent behaviors beyond human design intent or control, regardless of governance structures.

claims.statement: Ethical and intelligence failures in AI systems are fundamentally governance failures caused by human design choices rather than machine autonomy.

support.explanation: This passage directly supports the claim that obedience-related failures (AI following instructions) are grounded in the structure of the delegation rather than the machine's inherent intelligence or autonomy.
support.passage: Ethical failures associated with AI are best understood as governance failures rooted in human design choices and accountability arrangements, even where opacity and limited control complicate responsibility attribution.

actions.findings: Ethical and intelligence failures in AI systems are fundamentally governance failures caused by human design choices rather than machine autonomy. [source-f1c16003c47b4e8f]
actions.limitations: The current evidence base relies on historical and conceptual synthesis rather than empirical technical data from failures in contemporary deployed models.
actions.next_questions: What specific design patterns for override mechanisms effectively mitigate the delegation failures identified here?
actions.reason: The source identifies a fundamental shift in AI ethics: moving from 'autonomy' risks to 'delegation' failures.
actions.summary: AI ethics failures, often framed as problems of 'autonomy', are identified as instances of delegation failure where human accountability is displaced onto systems with bounded autonomy. Intelligence failures occur when these delegated instructions are executed without adequate override or design-level oversight.
actions.title: Delegation and Governance: Re-framing Obedience Failure
